name: Soldano SLO-100 Super Lead Overdrive
description: Soldano SLO-100 Super Lead Overdrive, 1996 factory drawing, complete: input stage, Crunch/Clean divider, clean and overdrive channels, LDR1/2/4/LDR3 channel and master switching, FX send buffer / FX return recovery, DC-coupled tone-stack cathode follower and the late-in-circuit JCM800-style stack, long-tail-pair phase inverter with 4-ohm-tap feedback, presence and depth, four 6L6GC, output transformer and the 16 ohm cab.

sources.title: Soldano SLO-100 factory schematic, drawn March 15 1996, sheet 1 of 2 (preamp, crunch/clean switching, FX loop, supply) and sheet 2 of 2 (tone stack, master volumes, LTP, power amp, footswitch/LDR box), R1-R70 / C1-C41 designators
sources.note: The PDF is an Acrobat image-conversion of a raster scan: pdfimages reports each page as a single 1995x1269 (sheet 1) / 2022x1084 (sheet 2) 8-bit image at 72 ppi, i.e. the source contains no more than that. Those native pixels are legible at 1:1 (68K, 0.02uF, 470K, 500K, 1M, 39K, 220K, 0.001 all read cleanly); rendering the page at 300 dpi only interpolates. Every value in this netlist was read from the native raster, not from a 300 dpi render.

sources.title: Rob Robinette, 'How the Soldano Super Lead Overdrive SLO-100 & 50 Watt Amplifiers Work' - annotated redraw of the same drawing (V2.6, 5068x2037, vector text) plus the SLO-Nakid redraw (4034x1828) and the article text
sources.note: Used as the independent second source for the OD chain, the attenuator values and the channel-switching functions: 'the first OD Channel divider is a 470k Attenuator resistor + the 500k OD Gain pot ... bypassed with a .002uF Treble Peaker'; 'a large 470k grid stop resistor'; 'a 470k + 1M attenuator dumps 32%'; 'the .001uF plate load bypass cap'; 'Soldano used a .001uF Bright cap' on the OD Gain pot; 'the Clean signal joins the Overdrive Channel at Preamp 4 with no mixing resistors'; 'in Overdrive Mode both the Clean and OD Channel signal paths are active'; 'LDR + and - : power on = LED on and switch closed'.

sources.title: Soldano SLO-100 annotated manual / errata copy (manualmachine)
sources.note: Production changes (FX recovery cathode bypass 25 uF, 1 k FX return load, plate-load bypass 0.001 uF).

sources.title: Soldano factory modification text ('slo100not.txt', pages 5-8 of the same el34world PDF)
sources.note: Confirms that the clean/crunch channel is also in circuit in lead mode and that its level is 'much lower'.

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS = 1.5 x the 143 V peak measured at the dimed OD channel (1.0 V in, 220 Hz, overdrive 1, master 1). The dimed Clean channel peaks at 68 V (43.4 V RMS into 16 ohm = 117 W); the OD channel is the larger of the two, so 214 V is the 1.5x figure for the amp.

VTL5C1_CELL.note: VTL5C1 CdS cell, PerkinElmer datasheet: 5 k / 600 / 200 ohm at 1 / 10 / 40 mA LED current, 50 Mohm dark, 2.5 ms on / 35 ms off. ron and gamma fitted to the three on-resistance points through this LED card (steady state 5.15 k / 555 / 210 ohm); the previous card (600 ohm at 2 mA) read 15.8 k / 900 / 246 ohm, i.e. 4.7 k at the old 2.4 mA drive

VTL5C1_LED.note: VTL5C1 LED, VTL5C3/2 Shockley card scaled to the 2 mA full-light reference

controls.label: Normal
controls.note: Clean channel gain: 500 k Clean Gain pot P2 after the Crunch/Clean attenuator

controls.label: Overdrive
controls.note: OD channel gain: 500 k OD Gain pot P1 between the V1A attenuator and V2A

controls.label: Channel
controls.note: OD = LDR2 & LDR3 on, LDR1 & LDR4 off; Clean = LDR1 & LDR4 on, LDR2 & LDR3 off. The LDRs are switch models here (no VTL5C1 card in the engine).

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: 1 M Bass pot in the late-in-circuit JCM800-style stack

controls.label: Master
controls.note: Master: drives both 1 M master pots (OD MV and Norm MV); the channel LDRs (LDR3 in OD, LDR4 in Clean) pass the active channel's wiper to the PI, so the knob works on both channels. The amp has one master per channel; the catalogue has one Master

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: 25 k-L presence rheostat with 0.1 uF from the feedback node to ground; up = less resistance = less treble feedback = more presence

controls.label: Depth
controls.note: Optional Depth/Resonance 1 M-A pot in series with the 4-ohm-tap feedback (with 0.1 uF and a 0.0047 uF bridge); the annotated drawing marks it optional. Up = less low-frequency feedback = more bass

controls.label: Crunch
controls.note: S1 Crunch/Clean. 0 (the position drawn on the 1996 sheet) = Clean: input 470 k + 470 k by 39 k divider, about 96 % of the signal dumped. 1 = Crunch: the extra 470 k bypassed and the 39 k shunt lifted, leaving only the 470 k into the Clean Gain pot (48 % dump). Independent of the Channel switch.

controls.label: Bright
controls.note: S2 Bright/Norm: Bright = 470 pF instead of the 470 k into the Clean Gain pot top (drawing: Bright off)

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Sag emerges from the supply; stored only

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: The bias is a rear trim; no front-panel control, stored only

parts.note: The SLO PT is a 120 VAC primary / 360 VAC HT winding into a bridge; the project's two-source full-wave equivalent is used (JCM800/5E3 convention). One diode drop instead of the bridge's two.

Choke DCR 60 Ohm (unverified: from the drawn 2 V plates-to-screens drop at ~32 mA)
Screens to B2 dropper 10 k 3 W (drawing: 497/495 V -> 378 V)

parts.note: The annotated drawing's bias network (220 k/15 k/10 k/25 k trim, 1N4007, 10 uF/100 V) is modelled as the filter node, as the JCM800/Plexi/AB763 netlists do, because a negative-peak rectifier is not charged at the mains-crest operating point used by --settle 0. -55 V is fitted so the library 6L6GC idles near 30 mA at 495 V.

parts.label: Clean-divider 39 k (in circuit only in the Clean throw, S1 pole 2)
S1 Clean throw: connects the 39 k divider shunt to ground (closed = Clean)
S1 Crunch throw: bypasses the 470 k extra divider resistor (closed = Crunch)
S2 Bright/Norm 470 pF: Bright throw (the cap feeds the Clean Gain pot top through SW_BRB)
S2 Bright throw: 470 pF into the Clean Gain pot top (closed = Bright)
470 k Normal-path resistor into the Clean Gain pot top (the divider that dumps 48%)
S2 Normal throw: 470 k into the Clean Gain pot top (closed = Bright off)
P2 Clean Gain 500 k; top fed from the Bright/Norm switch (470 k Normal path or 470 pF Bright path)
0.001 uF Bright cap across the OD Gain pot (top to wiper)
P1 OD Gain 500 k, top on the treble-peaker/switch node (V1b path), wiper through the 470 k grid stop
OD gain to V2A grid 470 k
V2A cathode 1.8 k (drawing "1.8K"), bypassed by C4
Cold-clipper grid 1 M (OD gain trim / LDR1 shunt)
0.02 uF cold-clipper coupling into the LDR2 anti-pop node
2.2 M anti-pop / grid leak on the LDR2 node (drawing: 2.2M Anti-Pop)
V3A FX buffer DC-coupled cathode follower (grid = V3B plate, plate on B2)
FX buffer cathode load 100 k
parts.note: Solver partition (cuts: k3a, loads R24): the V3A cathode follower's output splits the preamp (V1B-V3A) from the FX recovery, tone stack, PI and power amp, which were one 80-unknown / 39-port group. The follower's ~1/gm source drives only this 100 k into the 2.2 k send divider, so the one-sample lag is below the SPICE gate's resolution (slo_od 0.084 -> 0.085 %, slo_clean 0.050 % and slo_ac unchanged, slo_od_hot spk 0.78 % uncut -> 0.74 %; aliasing gate -64.5 -> -62.3 dB) and the live unit drops from about 135 % to about 81 % of one core on a guitar DI at 48 kHz (-27 % instructions; 2026-11-11). Before the split every audio callback overran. The V4A follower (k4a) is not cut: it drives the tone stack and cuts off on hard drive, and a cut there costs slo_od 0.08 -> 1.35 %.

parts.label: Soldano 100 W output transformer
parts.note: unverified: the drawing gives no Raa/DCR; 1.7 k p-p, 16 ohm tap turns 2*sqrt(16/1700), 4 ohm tap half of that; 20 ohm per half, 3 mH leakage, lm 80 H, lsat 5 V s are typical-class values. Feedback is taken from the 4 ohm tap (the drawing's note).

parts.label: Feedback 39 k into the feedback node; its far end goes through the 0.1 uF and the Depth network to the 4 ohm tap
Feedback-loop series 0.1 uF between the Depth network and the 39 k (Robinette's annotated SLO-100 redraw)
Presence 0.1 uF from the feedback node
Presence 25 k-L rheostat: 0.1 uF to the wiper, the clockwise lug to ground (1996 sheet 2), so the series resistance is 25k*(1-x) and full presence is 0 ohm (most treble taken out of the feedback)
Depth 0.0047 uF across the Depth pot, in series with the feedback from the 4 ohm tap

Depth 1 M-A rheostat in series with the feedback, bridged by 0.0047 uF (Robinette: 'removes low frequencies from the NFB loop'; marked optional). Resistance rises with rotation (audio taper from the ccw lug, as on the MK II drawing): 0 = full feedback, 1 = 1 M || 4.7 nF, least bass feedback
OD LED drive: 8.7 mA per LED, the footswitch circuit's OD state (switch open: 6 V reservoir -> 33 / 47 ohm -> 61.9 ohm -> VR2 || VR3 -> 33 ohm), as a 5 V Thevenin equivalent
OD channel LDR LED (2 mA)
parts.note: multirate.slow (12 kHz): the two LED drivers, their light nodes and the four cells' light history run every 16th sample at the 192 kHz unit rate (2026-11-11). They are constant at a fixed channel and were a quarter of the unit's cost (eight small Newton groups). The SPICE cases and the aliasing figure are unchanged; a channel switch's 20 ms crossfade stays within 3 dB per 2 ms window of the full-rate one, and the unit's median callback at 48 kHz / 128 on a guitar DI drops from about 2.2-2.3 to 1.8-2.0 ms against the 2.67 ms period (loaded machine).

parts.label: Clean LED drive: 34 mA per LED, the footswitch circuit's Clean state (switch closed: 6 V reservoir -> 33 / 47 ohm, 61.9 ohm across VR1 || VR4), as a 5 V Thevenin equivalent
LDR1 OD kill (lit in Clean, about 235 ohm at 34 mA)
LDR2 (VR2): cold-clipper output into the Clean/OD preamp-4 summing node a1 (lit in OD)
LDR3 (VR3) OD master select: OD MV wiper -> PI coupling (on in OD)
LDR4 (VR4) Normal master select: Norm MV wiper -> PI coupling (on in Clean)
Clean path 220 k grid stop into OD preamp 4 (always connected: the Clean channel is always on)
FX send load RL 2.2 k (send tap across it)
